Skin and Subcutaneous Tissue Disorders: pruritus, alopecia, a variety of skin changes (e.g., nodules, discoloration, dryness of skin/mucous membranes, changes to hair/nails), purpura, lichen planus, urticaria, photosensitivity, flushing, toxic epidermal necrolysis, erythema multiforme, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome

mechanism_of_action.value: Prodrug hydrolyzed to active beta-hydroxyacid form (simvastatin acid), which inhibits HMG-CoA reductase (rate-limiting enzyme converting HMG-CoA to mevalonate), accelerating hepatic LDL-receptor expression and lowering plasma LDL-C and VLDL.

refs.quote: Simvastatin is a prodrug and is hydrolyzed to its active β-hydroxyacid form, simvastatin acid, after administration. Simvastatin acid and its metabolites are inhibitors of HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme that converts HMG-CoA to mevalonate, a precursor of cholesterol.

refs.locator: 7.1 Drug Interactions that Increase the Risk of Myopathy and Rhabdomyolysis
refs.quote: ZOCOR is a substrate of CYP3A4 and of the transport protein OATP1B1. ZOCOR exposure can be significantly increased with concomitant administration of inhibitors of CYP3A4 and OATP1B1.

value.drug_or_class: Strong CYP3A4 Inhibitors (itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, voriconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin, HIV/HCV protease inhibitors, cobicistat, nefazodone)
value.effect: Markedly increases simvastatin exposure (up to >10-fold), increasing risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
value.management: Concomitant use is contraindicated; if strong CYP3A4 inhibitor treatment is unavoidable, suspend ZOCOR during the course.

refs.quote: Intervention: Concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with ZOCOR is contraindicated [see Contraindications (4) ] . If treatment with a CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, suspend ZOCOR during the course of strong CYP3A4 inhibitor treatment.

value.effect: Increases risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
value.management: Concomitant use of cyclosporine, danazol, or gemfibrozil with ZOCOR is contraindicated.

refs.quote: Intervention: Concomitant use of cyclosporine, danazol, or gemfibrozil with ZOCOR is contraindicated [see Contraindications (4) ] .

value.effect: Increases simvastatin exposure and risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
value.management: Do not exceed ZOCOR 10 mg daily.

refs.quote: Intervention: For patients taking verapamil, diltiazem, or dronedarone, do not exceed ZOCOR 10 mg daily.

value.effect: Increases simvastatin exposure and risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
value.management: Do not exceed ZOCOR 20 mg daily.

refs.quote: For patients taking amiodarone, amlodipine, or ranolazine, do not exceed ZOCOR 20 mg daily [see Dosage and Administration (2.5) ] .

value.effect: Simvastatin exposure is approximately doubled, increasing risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
value.management: Reduce ZOCOR dose by 50% when initiating lomitapide; do not exceed 20 mg daily (or 40 mg daily for patients chronically on 80 mg).

refs.quote: Intervention: Reduce the dose of ZOCOR by 50% if initiating lomitapide. Do not exceed ZOCOR 20 mg daily (or ZOCOR 40 mg daily for patients who have previously taken an 80 mg daily dosage of ZOCOR chronically)

value.effect: Cases of rhabdomyolysis reported when simvastatin was administered with daptomycin.
value.management: If treatment with daptomycin is required, consider temporarily suspending ZOCOR during daptomycin treatment.

refs.quote: Intervention: If treatment with daptomycin is required, consider temporarily suspending ZOCOR during the course of daptomycin treatment.

value.effect: Grapefruit juice can raise plasma levels of simvastatin (up to 7-16 fold at high dose) and increase risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
value.management: Avoid grapefruit juice when taking ZOCOR.

refs.quote: Grapefruit Juice Clinical Impact: Grapefruit juice can raise the plasma levels of simvastatin and may increase the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Intervention: Avoid grapefruit juice when taking ZOCOR.

value.effect: Cases of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis observed with lipid-modifying dosages of niacin; higher risk in Chinese patients (1.24% myopathy).
value.management: Not recommended in Chinese patients; in non-Chinese patients, weigh benefit vs risk and monitor for myopathy.

refs.quote: Cases of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis have been observed with concomitant use of lipid modifying dosages of niacin-containing products (≥1 gram/day niacin) with ZOCOR. The risk of myopathy is greater in Chinese patients.

value.effect: Increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
value.management: Weigh benefit vs risk; monitor for signs and symptoms of myopathy, especially during initiation and upward dose titration.

refs.quote: Colchicine Clinical Impact: Cases of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis have been reported with concomitant use of colchicine with ZOCOR. Intervention: Consider if the benefit of using colchicine concomitantly with ZOCOR outweighs the increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.

value.effect: May potentiate anticoagulant effect and increase INR; bleeding reported.
value.management: Obtain INR before starting ZOCOR and monitor INR frequently after initiation, dose titration, or discontinuation until stable.

refs.quote: Intervention: In patients taking coumarin anticoagulants, obtain an INR before starting ZOCOR and frequently enough after initiation, dose titration, or discontinuation to ensure that no significant alteration in INR occurs.

value.effect: Concomitant use may result in elevated plasma digoxin concentrations.
value.management: Monitor digoxin levels when ZOCOR is initiated.

refs.quote: Digoxin Clinical Impact: Concomitant use of digoxin with ZOCOR may result in elevated plasma digoxin concentrations [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] . Intervention: Monitor digoxin levels in patients taking digoxin when ZOCOR is initiated.

tier.note: PLLR Pregnancy section explicitly states 'Discontinue ZOCOR when pregnancy is recognized' because simvastatin decreases synthesis of cholesterol and biologically active cholesterol derivatives and may cause fetal harm, while hyperlipidemia treatment is generally unnecessary during pregnancy.

refs.quote: Discontinue ZOCOR when pregnancy is recognized. Alternatively, consider the ongoing therapeutic needs of the individual patient. ZOCOR decreases synthesis of cholesterol and possibly other biologically active substances derived from cholesterol; therefore, ZOCOR may cause fetal harm when administered to pregnant patients based on the mechanism of action
